source.title: Tame topology of arithmetic quotients and algebraicity of Hodge loci
source.authors: Benjamin Bakker, Bruno Klingler, Jacob Tsimerman
source.venue: Journal of the American Mathematical Society33(2020),917–939
readSections: Entire author copy: pages1–23, §§1–5, AppendixA and references.
Entire four-page official correction, including compact-choice, morphism and rational-Siegel-pullback corrections.
source.version: Full author PDF read together with official erratum (JAMS36(2023), DOI10.1090/jams/1025). Published metadata checked; full typeset collation remains G1.

summary: The corrected paper gives fixed-maximal-compact semialgebraic arithmetic quotient structures and compatible morphisms, finite Siegel containment for period maps, R_an,exp definability of period maps on algebraic bases and algebraicity of individual exceptional Hodge-locus components. This partial extraction imports existing Hodge carriers and reduction/variation owners, proposes two Part II extensions, and records the remaining source and proof-interface gaps.

items.name: Existing pure Hodge structure
items.statement: On a complex vector space W with conjugation ω, a weight-k pure Hodge structure is an exhaustive decreasing filtration F with F^p complementary to the conjugate of F^(k+1−p). The integral specialization uses a lattice and its complexification.

api.name: BKT.PureHodge.pieceDecomposition
api.statement: Recover F^a as the direct sum of H^(p,k−p) with p≥a.

api.name: BKT.PureHodge.conjugatePiece
api.statement: Conjugation sends H^(p,k−p) to H^(k−p,p).

api.name: BKT.PureHodge.shiftWeight
api.statement: A Tate shift by m has weight k−2m and filtration F^(p+m).

uses.how: Specify fibrewise opposed filtrations with the same weight.

unitTests.name: BKT.PureHodge.test1
unitTests.statement: The rank-one type (0,0) reconstructs its two-step filtration.

unitTests.name: BKT.PureHodge.test2
unitTests.statement: An effective rank-two weight-one structure exchanges (1,0) and (0,1).

unitTests.name: BKT.PureHodge.test3
unitTests.statement: An opposedness check rejects a rank-one purported odd-weight real structure.

items.name: Existing module-valued local system
items.statement: An R-module local coefficient system on a topological space X is a functor from its fundamental groupoid to ModuleCat R. For the integral PVHS consumer the fibres must additionally be finite free Z-modules; the generic carrier alone imposes neither freeness nor finiteness.

api.name: BKT.LocalSystem.transportIdentity
api.statement: Transport along the constant path is the identity.

api.name: BKT.LocalSystem.transportCompose

api.name: BKT.LocalSystem.finiteFreeFibres
api.statement: A PVHS adapter explicitly requires each integral fibre finite free; this is additional to LocalCoefficientSystem.

uses.how: Supply flat integral fibres and monodromy transport.

unitTests.name: BKT.LocalSystem.test1

unitTests.name: BKT.LocalSystem.test2

unitTests.name: BKT.LocalSystem.test3

items.name: Existing polarized period-domain point
items.statement: Fix a finite free Z-lattice V, its complexification, integral bilinear form Q, weight k and a finite-support symmetric Hodge type. A point is a Hodge filtration of that type polarized by Q. This carrier does not provide topology or a complex manifold.

api.name: BKT.PeriodPoint.filtrationExt
api.statement: Two period points with equal filtrations are equal.

api.name: BKT.PeriodPoint.hodgeRanks
api.statement: The prescribed Hodge dimensions sum to the complex dimension.

api.name: BKT.PeriodPoint.fixedPolarization
api.statement: The same input integral form polarizes every point; changing the form changes the parameter, not a field of the point.

uses.how: Retain the existing fixed-polarization carrier under the manifold realization.

unitTests.name: BKT.PeriodPoint.test1
unitTests.statement: A standard polarized elliptic Hodge filtration yields a point.

unitTests.name: BKT.PeriodPoint.test2
unitTests.statement: A Hodge type whose total dimension is wrong cannot yield a point.

unitTests.name: BKT.PeriodPoint.test3
unitTests.statement: Negating the standard weight-one polarization without changing the filtration fails positivity.

items.name: Existing Weil operator
items.statement: For a weight-k pure Hodge structure, C is the complex-linear endomorphism acting by i^(p−q) on H^(p,q), where p+q=k.

api.name: BKT.WeilOperator.onPiece
api.statement: C acts on H^(p,q) by i^(p−q).

api.name: BKT.WeilOperator.square
api.statement: C²=(−1)^k times the identity in weight k.

api.name: BKT.WeilOperator.realCompatibility
api.statement: C commutes with conjugation on the real form.

unitTests.name: BKT.WeilOperator.test2

unitTests.name: BKT.WeilOperator.test3

items.name: Existing Hermitian Hodge form
items.statement: For a polarization Q, the pinned library form is h_lib(u,v)=Q(C(conj u),v), conjugate-linear in u and linear in v. It equals the complex conjugate of the paper convention h_BKT(u,v)=Q(Cu,conj v). Diagonal real norms agree.

api.name: BKT.HodgeForm.conventionConjugate
api.statement: h_lib(u,v)=conj(h_BKT(u,v)) with the displayed Weil and polarization conventions.

api.name: BKT.HodgeForm.diagonalAgreement
api.statement: h_lib(u,u)=h_BKT(u,u) is real.

api.name: BKT.HodgeForm.sesquilinearity
api.statement: h_lib(au,bv)=conj(a)b h_lib(u,v).

uses.how: Use diagonal norms while reconciling conjugation conventions.

unitTests.name: BKT.HodgeForm.test1
unitTests.statement: For a normalized u, h_lib(iu,u)=−i while h_BKT(iu,u)=i.

unitTests.name: BKT.HodgeForm.test2
unitTests.statement: Diagonal scaling by i preserves the norm.

unitTests.name: BKT.HodgeForm.test3
unitTests.statement: The zero vector has zero norm and is excluded from strict positivity.

items.name: Existing positivity of the Hodge form
items.statement: For any polarization P and nonzero vector u in the complexification, P.hodgeForm(u,u)>0. In particular its real restriction is positive definite. Nonzero u is essential.
proofSteps: Import the pinned positivity theorem; convert the sesquilinear convention using hodge-form.

items.name: Existing rational mixed Hodge structure
items.statement: On compatible rational and complex models of an integral module, a mixed Hodge structure consists of a finite increasing rational weight filtration W and finite decreasing complex Hodge filtration F for which gr^W_k with its induced F is pure of weight k.

api.name: BKT.MixedHodge.gradedPure
api.statement: The k-th rational weight graded with its induced F is pure of weight k.

api.name: BKT.MixedHodge.rationalWeight
api.statement: Complex weights are complexifications of rational subspaces and are conjugation-stable.

api.name: BKT.MixedHodge.pureAsMixed
api.statement: A pure weight-k structure defines a mixed structure with only gr_k nonzero.

uses.how: Package the shifted monodromy filtration and limiting F.

unitTests.name: BKT.MixedHodge.test2
unitTests.statement: A split sum of weights zero and two has the prescribed two gradeds.

unitTests.name: BKT.MixedHodge.test3
unitTests.statement: Putting a weight-zero F on a nonzero gr_2 is rejected.

items.name: Existing Deligne bigrading
items.statement: For a mixed Hodge structure, I^(p,q)=(F^p∩W_(p+q))∩((conj F^q∩W_(p+q))+Σ_(j≥2)(conj F^(q−j+1)∩W_(p+q−j))). The weights here use the actual mixed weight; centered monodromy indices require a shift by the pure weight.

api.name: BKT.DeligneBigrading.recoverF
api.statement: F^a is the sum of I^(p,q) for p≥a.

api.name: BKT.DeligneBigrading.recoverW
api.statement: W_k is the sum of I^(p,q) for p+q≤k.

api.name: BKT.DeligneBigrading.conjugateModuloLower
api.statement: conj I^(p,q) equals I^(q,p) modulo pieces with first index<q and second index<p.

uses.how: Import the one-filtration decomposition without assuming the multi-filtration extension.

unitTests.name: BKT.DeligneBigrading.test1
unitTests.statement: In a pure structure I^(p,q) equals its Hodge piece.

unitTests.name: BKT.DeligneBigrading.test2
unitTests.statement: A real-split mixed example has exact conjugation symmetry.

unitTests.name: BKT.DeligneBigrading.test3
unitTests.statement: A non-real-split extension must satisfy only the lower-term congruence, not exact symmetry.

items.name: Existing direct-sum and filtration recovery
items.statement: The I^(p,q) form an internal direct sum of the underlying complex vector space. F^p∩W_k is the sum of the pieces I^(r,s) with r≥p and r+s≤k. This concerns one mixed Hodge structure, not simultaneous splittings of several monodromy filtrations.
proofSteps: Use the pinned internal direct sum and simultaneous F/W truncation theorem.

items.name: Existing finite exponential of a nilpotent
items.statement: For a nilpotent a in a Q-algebra with a^m=0, exp_nil(a)=Σ_(0≤j<m) a^j/j!. Commuting nilpotents a,b satisfy exp_nil(a+b)=exp_nil(a)exp_nil(b). The analytic exponential comparison is a separate interface if needed.

api.name: BKT.NilpotentExp.truncate
api.statement: If N^m=0, exp_nil(zN)=Σ_(j<m) z^j N^j/j!.

api.name: BKT.NilpotentExp.commutingSum
api.statement: For commuting nilpotents A,B, exp_nil(A+B)=exp_nil(A)exp_nil(B).

api.name: BKT.NilpotentExp.inverse
api.statement: exp_nil(N)exp_nil(−N)=1.

uses.how: Use a finite algebraic polynomial for monodromy twists.

unitTests.name: BKT.NilpotentExp.test2

unitTests.name: BKT.NilpotentExp.test3

items.name: Expansions of the ordered real field
items.statement: A structure consists of Boolean algebras of subsets of R^n containing semialgebraic sets and closed under products and coordinate projections; parameters from R are allowed. A function is definable when its graph is definable.

api.name: BKT.RealDefinableStructure.project

api.name: BKT.RealDefinableStructure.boolean

items.name: O-minimality
items.statement: An expansion of the ordered real field is o-minimal if every definable subset of R is a finite union of points and intervals.

api.name: BKT.OMinimal.discreteFinite

items.name: Restricted analytic functions
items.statement: A real function is restricted analytic when it agrees on a fixed compact box with an analytic function on an open neighborhood of that box and is zero outside it. Rescaling compact boxes does not change the generated structure.

api.name: BKT.RestrictedAnalytic.rescaleBox
api.statement: Affine rescaling between compact boxes preserves restricted analyticity.

api.name: BKT.RestrictedAnalytic.complexComponents

items.name: The structures R_alg, R_an, R_exp and R_an,exp
items.statement: R_alg is the real semialgebraic structure; R_an adds restricted real analytic functions; R_exp adds real exponential; R_an,exp adds both. Inclusions of structures preserve definability; none identifies the Borel–Serre and algebraic structures without a comparison.

api.name: BKT.TameStructures.analyticToCombined

api.name: BKT.TameStructures.realExpDefinable

items.name: O-minimality of the required real expansions
items.statement: R_alg, R_an, R_exp and R_an,exp are o-minimal. The R_an case uses Gabrielov/van den Dries and the combined case uses van den Dries–Miller; the combined assertion is not inferred merely from o-minimality of its two reducts.

items.name: Definable manifolds with finite atlas
items.statement: A paracompact Hausdorff space has a definable manifold structure if it has a finite cover by coordinate neighborhoods with definable chart images, overlaps and transition homeomorphisms. Structures are identified when mixed transitions are definable.

api.statement: Finite definable refinements produce the same definable subsets.

api.name: BKT.FiniteDefinableAtlas.graphCriterion
api.statement: A map is definable iff its graph is definable in all pairs of charts.

api.name: BKT.FiniteDefinableAtlas.finiteGlue

uses.how: Provide finite graph checks independent of charts.

unitTests.name: BKT.FiniteDefinableAtlas.test3

items.name: Definable images, pullbacks and finite gluing
items.statement: Graphs of maps between finite definable atlases define maps independently of the atlas. Composition, finite products, images and inverse images are definable; maps that agree on a finite definable cover glue definably. Descent through a definable surjection holds by projecting the graph of the composite.
proofSteps: Translate each claim into finite Boolean operations and coordinate projection.
For descent, existentially quantify a source representative; constancy on fibres supplies a well-defined graph.

items.name: Real analytic manifolds with corners
items.statement: Charts are homeomorphisms from relatively open subsets of [0,∞)^r×R^(n−r) to open subsets of a paracompact Hausdorff space. Transitions and their inverses extend real analytically to ambient open neighborhoods. Weakly analytic maps are continuous maps satisfying this extension property in charts.

api.statement: The depth-zero locus is a real analytic n-manifold.

api.name: BKT.AnalyticCorners.ambientExtension
api.statement: Each chart transition has an analytic extension on an ambient neighborhood.

api.name: BKT.AnalyticCorners.depthInvariant

items.name: Boundary with local branches
items.statement: The boundary of an n-manifold with corners consists of pairs (x,b), where b is a local codimension-one boundary component at x. It is an (n−1)-manifold with corners with a weakly analytic immersion i_X to X; i_X need not be injective at corners.

items.statement: Use finite atlases as for finite-definable-atlas, now with definable relatively open orthant domains; overlap homeomorphisms are definable. Definable subsets and graphs are tested in every chart. No ambient smoothness is built into this topological definability carrier.

items.name: Compact analytic corners admit a canonical R_an structure
items.statement: A compact real analytic manifold with corners admits a canonical R_an-definable structure compatible with its analytic atlas. Independence means definable identity between constructions using different finite buffered chart covers.
proofSteps: Shrink analytic coordinate boxes with closures inside larger coordinate neighborhoods.
Compactness supplies a finite cover; restricted analytic transitions on the buffered closures are definable.
Use a common finite refinement to prove independence. Relative compactness alone without extension control is insufficient.

items.name: Definability of boundary immersion and interior
items.statement: For compact analytic X with corners and its canonical R_an structure, the boundary-branch immersion i_X is R_an-definable, and X minus its image is a definable manifold.
proofSteps: Apply the same finite buffered atlas construction to the compact boundary.
Locally the immersion inserts a zero coordinate, so its graph is definable; take its image and complement.

items.name: Cartan involutions and maximal compact subgroups
items.statement: For a connected real reductive group, a Cartan involution determines its maximal compact fixed subgroup K and a Cartan decomposition. In the arithmetic application choose K containing the given connected compact subgroup M; its conjugates give the symmetric space of maximal compact subgroups.

api.name: BKT.CartanMaximalCompact.conjugateChoice

api.name: BKT.CartanMaximalCompact.containsCompact
api.statement: For a compact subgroup M in a real linear reductive group, choose maximal compact K containing M.

uses.how: Retain K and its Cartan involution as parameters of every Siegel construction.

items.name: Arithmetic quotient with chosen compact data
items.statement: Let Gbold be connected semisimple over Q, G=Gbold(R)^+, Γ⊂Gbold(Q)∩G torsion-free arithmetic, M⊂G connected compact, and K⊃M maximal compact. items.name: Morphisms compatible with chosen maximal compacts
items.statement: A morphism from (Γ′,G′,M′,K′) to (Γ,G,M,K) is induced by a Q-group map φ and g∈G, via Γ′h′M′↦Γφ(h′)gM, with φΓ′⊂Γ, φM′⊂gMg⁻¹, φK′⊂gKg⁻¹, and the Cartan involution for gKg⁻¹ stabilizing dφ(g′). Definability is a conclusion, not an extra assumed property of this data.

items.name: Rational parabolic and horospherical data
items.statement: For a rational parabolic P of Gbold, let N_P be its unipotent radical and L_P its Levi quotient. Let A_P be the positive real component of the maximal Q-split central torus of L_P, and M_P the intersection of kernels of squares of its Q-characters on real points. A chosen K selects a Cartan-stable real Levi lift, not necessarily defined over Q, and G=N_P A_P M_P K in horospherical coordinates.

api.name: BKT.RationalParabolicData.leviQuotient
api.statement: P/N_P is the rational reductive Levi quotient.

api.name: BKT.RationalParabolicData.cartanLift
api.statement: K specifies a real Cartan-stable lift of that quotient.

items.name: Translation and conjugation rules with compact data
items.statement: Conjugation by g carries a Siegel set for (P,K) to one for (gPg⁻¹,gKg⁻¹). Right translation by real g carries the fixed-P construction to compact g⁻¹Kg; rational left translations can be represented as Siegel sets with the original K and a changed rational parabolic. Retain the coordinate identifications in each rule.
proofSteps: Use the parabolic horospherical decomposition and conjugation of the Cartan involution.
Distinguish right translation, conjugation, and rational left translation; no independence of K follows.

items.name: Finite arithmetic cover by fixed-K Siegel sets
items.statement: There are finitely many Γ-conjugacy classes of rational parabolics and finitely many associated semialgebraic Siegel sets, all using the chosen K, whose images cover Γ\G/M.
proofSteps: Use the rational reduction theorem with fixed compact data and project the finite cover to G/M.

items.name: Finite arithmetic overlaps of Siegel sets
items.statement: For any two Siegel sets S₁,S₂ associated to the same K, the set of γ∈Γ with γS₁∩S₂ nonempty is finite. The property extends to relatively compact closures of their unipotent and Levi factors.
proofSteps: Apply the rational Siegel property, also for the enlarged compact factors.

items.name: Separation of inequivalent cusps
items.statement: If P₁ and P₂ are not Γ-conjugate, then for fixed bounded U_i,W_i and sufficiently large truncation parameters t_i, γS₁∩S₂ is empty for every γ∈Γ. All Siegel data use one K.
proofSteps: Use the cusp separation part of rational reduction theory.

items.name: Deep self-intersections come from the parabolic
items.statement: For fixed U,W and sufficiently large t, a Siegel set S for P and K satisfies γS∩S=∅ whenever γ∈Γ\(Γ∩P).
proofSteps: Apply parabolic separation to the deep positive chamber.

items.name: Deep corners for distinct parabolics separate
items.statement: For distinct rational parabolics P₁≠P₂ and fixed bounded factors using one K, the corresponding Siegel sets are disjoint once both truncation parameters are sufficiently large.
proofSteps: Use the final separation assertion of the fixed-K reduction theorem.

items.name: Semialgebraic model of G/M

proofSteps: Use the semialgebraic compact-group equivalence relation on G×G.
Its definably proper quotient gives the model and projection; multiplication descends to the action.
Alternatively use a faithful orbit with compact stabilizer and finite invariant polynomials. The original external quotient/invariant-theory proofs remain source leaves.

items.statement: For a closed semialgebraic equivalence relation on a semialgebraic set whose coordinate projections are definably proper in the sense of van den Dries Chapter10, the topological quotient has the corresponding semialgebraic quotient structure. items.name: Definable structure on an arithmetic quotient with K
items.statement: For every torsion-free arithmetic Γ and connected compact M⊂K as above, Γ\G/M has an R_alg-definable manifold structure characterized by definability of π restricted to every semialgebraic Siegel set associated to K. On finitely many buffered compact charts the quotient corner maps are restricted analytic.
Compare the resulting atlases; no semialgebraic assertion for every boundary transition is made.

items.name: Corrected containment of subgroup Siegel sets
items.statement: Let H⊂G be reductive Q-groups and S_H a Siegel set for a triple (P_H,A_H,K_H). For a fixed maximal compact K_G containing K_H, assume its Cartan involution stabilizes the split torus A_H. Then S_H is contained in finitely many G(Q)-translates of a Siegel set for K_G. The triples can be chosen with R_u(P_H)⊂R_u(P_G) and A_H=A_G∩H.
items.locator: Orr–Schnell2023 Theorem1; replacing the fixed-K use of originalTheorem3.2
proofSteps: Use the corrected Cartan-stable torus condition in Orr’s Lemma4.4.
Then apply the remaining original reduction proof with the additional minor corrections from Orr–Schnell§E.
The correction proof is read; the full original Orr proof remains a gap.

items.name: Subgroup stability is a sufficient stronger condition
items.statement: If K_H⊂K_G and θ_(K_G) stabilizes H, its restriction is the Cartan involution for H and stabilizes the split torus of an H-Siegel triple. Thus the corrected containment theorem applies. The converse implication from torus stability to subgroup stability is false.
proofSteps: Restrict the Cartan involution and use uniqueness of the Cartan-stable split torus in the chosen minimal parabolic.

items.name: Rational Siegel intersection with a subgroup
items.statement: Let H⊂G be reductive over Q, K_H=K_G∩H(R) maximal compact, and assume every K_H-Siegel set lies in finitely many G(Q)-translates of some K_G-Siegel set. For every K_G-Siegel set S_G there are a K_H-Siegel set S_H and finite F⊂H(Q) with S_G∩H(R)⊂F S_H.
proofSteps: Choose Γ_H=Γ_G∩H and a finite rational-cusp cover H(R)=Γ_H C_H S_H.
Enlarge S_G after rationally aligning the minimal parabolics so the assumed forward containment is S_H⊂A S_G for finite rational A.
The Siegel property bounds the γ with S_G∩γ C_H A S_G nonempty. Those finitely many γC_H give F.
items.note: The forward containment hypothesis is part of the statement. Borel–Harish-Chandra7.5 for real Siegel domains is not substituted here.

items.name: Dependence on maximal compact is real
items.statement: For G=SL₂ and M={1}, distinct maximal compacts K_x,K_y yield distinct definable structures on Γ\G. The overlap fibre product of corresponding Siegel sets has infinitely many connected components, excluding a definable identity map in an o-minimal structure.
proofSteps: Reduce to K_y fixing i in the upper half-plane.
K_x i is a nontrivial circle; positive diagonal scaling produces unbounded horizontal coordinate, incompatible with finite K_y-Siegel coverage.
Use the resulting infinite overlap components as the definability obstruction.

items.name: Compact inclusion alone does not imply Siegel containment
items.statement: There are reductive, and also semisimple, rational subgroup inclusions with K_H⊂K_G for which an H-Siegel set is not covered by finitely many rational translates of K_G-Siegel sets. Therefore the Cartan compatibility cannot be deleted from the definable-morphism interface.
proofSteps: For the conjugate split torus in SL₂, its orbit in H is the diagonal ray (1−y)+iy, escaping all finite rational cusp-strip covers.
The SL₃ conjugate orthogonal example gives the semisimple obstruction: fixed compact subgroup but a conjugating matrix with non-diagonal ηᵗη.
Use the source’s parabolic-intersection lemma for the latter contradiction.

items.name: Hodge morphisms preserve the canonical compact data
items.statement: For a rational Hodge morphism φ with φ∘t′=g t g⁻¹ and φΓ′⊂Γ, the induced map of Lie algebras is a Hodge morphism. It sends K_(t′) into gK_tg⁻¹ and its image is stable under the latter Cartan involution. The resulting map of pure Hodge manifolds is R_alg-definable.

items.name: Finite buffered charts near a normal-crossing boundary
items.statement: A smooth complex quasi-projective S has a smooth projective compactification with simple normal-crossing boundary. A finite cover by sufficiently small coordinate polydisks, whose closures lie inside larger analytic coordinate neighborhoods, reduces the period-map problem to smaller punctured polydisks times disks.
proofSteps: Import characteristic-zero compactification and resolution with its exact boundary statement.
Use compactness to choose a finite buffered analytic cover.
Retain the smaller-disk restriction; holomorphic functions on an unbuffered open unit disk need not be definable near its outer boundary.

items.name: Quasi-unipotence of local monodromy
items.statement: The integral monodromy operators of a polarized variation around the coordinates of a punctured polydisk commute and have roots of unity as eigenvalues. Finite coordinate power covers make all of them unipotent.
proofSteps: Borel’s metric argument brings the conjugacy class arbitrarily close to a compact stabilizer, so eigenvalues have absolute value one.
Integrality and the same property for all conjugates allow Kronecker’s theorem.
Take a common multiple of the finite semisimple orders and pull back along power maps.

items.name: Holomorphic extension of the untwisted map
items.statement: For a polarized variation on a punctured polydisk with unipotent monodromy, Ψ extends holomorphically to the full polydisk with values in Dcheck. Its limiting filtration F=Ψ(0) defines a nilpotent orbit. Auxiliary unpunctured variables are allowed on relatively compact subdisks.

items.name: Definability of the punctured-disk covering on a sector
items.statement: On a bounded real strip, z↦exp(2πiz) has R_an,exp-definable real and imaginary parts: e^(−2πy) times restricted sine and cosine in x. A finite set of overlapping strips covers the punctured disk of any fixed smaller radius.

items.name: Definability of the lifted local period map

Compose the restricted analytic extension Ψ with the sector exponential, then use the algebraic action on Dcheck.
Restrict to the semialgebraic locus D.

items.name: Closure laws for rough functions
items.statement: Roughly monomial functions are stable under products and reciprocals. Roughly polynomial functions form a ring and are stable under division by a roughly monomial function. The comparison constants and sector are retained in each operation.
proofSteps: Multiply the two-sided bounds for monomials and use common nonvanishing denominators for sums.

items.name: Curve test for a global rough-polynomial bound
items.statement: Let f be roughly polynomial and g roughly monomial on Σ_n. Suppose |f|≤C_τ|g| on every nonempty intersection with a complex affine curve α₁z₁+β₁=⋯=α_(n₀)z_(n₀)+β_(n₀), remaining coordinates fixed in H, for each 1≤n₀≤n, positive rational α_i and real β_i. Then one constant C bounds |f|/|g| on all Σ_n.
proofSteps: Clear roughly monomial denominators and reduce to a Laurent polynomial bounded relative to one monomial.
Taylor-expand the restricted analytic coefficients in q₁; the discarded terms decay exponentially relative to all required monomials on the ordered sector.
Eliminate positive powers of y₁ using fixed-tail curves, then use finitely many rational slopes and real offsets to isolate coefficients by interpolation and induct on n.
items.note: The printed substitutions z₁=mz₂+i can leave 0<Re z₁<1. A buffered/subdivided-horizontal-strip interpolation lemma must justify those steps; this proof-interface gap remains explicit.

items.name: Centered monodromy weight filtration
items.statement: For a nilpotent N on a finite-dimensional rational vector space, W(N) is the unique finite increasing filtration with N W_j⊂W_(j−2) and N^j:gr^W_j≅gr^W_(−j) for j≥0. It is centered at zero; for a weight-k limiting mixed Hodge structure the actual weights are shifted by k.

items.name: Constancy of monodromy weights on cone interiors
items.statement: For commuting nilpotents defining a polarized nilpotent orbit, every strictly positive combination of the nilpotents in a fixed nonempty face has the same centered monodromy weight filtration W(face). Faces with different sets of generators may have different filtrations.

items.name: Limiting mixed Hodge structure
items.statement: For the limiting F=Ψ(0) and N in the interior of the full monodromy cone, (F,W(N)[k]) is a mixed Hodge structure polarized in the nilpotent-orbit sense. The existing generic MixedHodgeStructure carrier is used; existence is a degeneration theorem.

items.name: Distributivity needed for simultaneous splittings
items.statement: For the limiting filtration F of a polarized nilpotent orbit and any nested sequence of nilpotent-generator subsets, F together with their monodromy weight filtrations is a distributive family and admits a common adapted splitting over C. The rational weight subfamily admits a rational splitting.
proofSteps: Use the Cattani–Kaplan real-split replacement commuting with the nilpotents and inducing identity on the graded full weight filtration.
Induct on the number of nested faces; the two Hodge grading operators preserve the remaining weight filtrations.
Split the induced distributive subfamilies on each graded piece.

items.name: Asymptotic norm of a nonzero split flat vector
items.statement: For nonzero u∈J_(s₁,…,s_n)⊗C, h_z(u,u) is bounded above and below by positive constant multiples of (y₁/y₂)^s₁⋯(y_(n−1)/y_n)^s_(n−1)y_n^s_n on the ordered sector after the standard shrinking. Constants may depend on u and the variation.

items.statement: For F=Ψ(0), the Deligne splitting of the limiting adjoint mixed Hodge structure gives a complement to the filtration stabilizer: the sum of pieces with first Hodge index p<0. items.name: Triangular form of the horizontal perturbation
items.statement: For negative-lie-chart, Griffiths transversality implies v(q)=Σ_i q_i v_i(q_i,…,q_n), with [N_j,v_i]=0 for j<i. Consequently g(q)=1+Σ_i q_i g_i(q), where g_i preserves every earlier monodromy filtration W(M_j), j<i.
proofSteps: Write the logarithmic derivative identity using the regular power series (1−exp(−ad v))/(ad v).
Compare the negative Hodge components and expand in the boundary coordinates successively.
Translate commutation with earlier nilpotents into preservation of their weight filtrations.
items.note: The source gives this implication briefly; the coefficient-recursion proof and its uniform holomorphic bounds remain explicit tasks.

items.name: Exponential decay against ordered-sector powers
items.statement: Fix integer exponents on y_i,…,y_n with y_i≥⋯≥y_n≥1. The product e^(−4πy_i) times any such Laurent monomial tends uniformly to zero as y_n→∞. Negative powers are bounded by one and positive powers by a fixed power of y_i.
proofSteps: Bound the monomial by y_i^A for a fixed nonnegative A.
Use exponential decay of e^(−4πt)t^A uniformly on t≥Y as Y→∞.

items.name: Comparison with the nilpotent-orbit frame
items.statement: For nonzero u in a fixed simultaneous weight component, h_z(γ(z)u,γ(z)u) is comparable to h_z(exp(Σz_iN_i)u,exp(Σz_iN_i)u) on a sufficiently deep ordered sector. The estimate is uniform over compact parameter sets with the stated splitting data.
proofSteps: Each q_i g_i preserves the earlier weights; apply the norm estimates to bound the error by the main monomial times e^(−4πy_i) and a monomial in the remaining variables.
Make the relative error norm smaller than a fixed number below one by increasing the minimum height.
Apply the triangle and reverse triangle inequalities for the positive Hodge norm.

items.name: Flag adapted to the Hodge filtration
items.statement: Choose an ordered basis w_i of the simultaneous complex splitting with decreasing first Hodge index p_i, and let K_i=span(w₁,…,w_i). The transported flag γK_i refines the varying Hodge filtration. Write B(u,v)=Q(u,conj v), which is generally indefinite.

items.name: Nonvanishing of the adapted Gram minors
items.statement: For hodge-adapted-flag, B restricts nondegenerately to each γK_i. Its Gram determinant Δ_i=B(γ(w₁∧⋯∧w_i),γ(w₁∧⋯∧w_i)) is nonzero. Within each successive pure Hodge piece B has the scalar phase prescribed by the polarization.
proofSteps: Successively decompose along the orthogonal Hodge pieces.
On a fixed Hodge piece the appropriate phase multiple of B is positive definite, so refining the flag cannot introduce a degenerate restriction.
items.note: Ordinary positive-inner-product Gram–Schmidt cannot be applied directly to the indefinite form B.

items.name: Gram determinant and projection identities
items.statement: Let wtilde_i be B-orthogonalized γw_i along the adapted flag and set Δ₀=1. Then B(wtilde_i,wtilde_i)=Δ_i/Δ_(i−1). For any u, B(u,wtilde_i)=B(γ(w₁∧⋯∧w_(i−1))∧u,γ(w₁∧⋯∧w_i))/Δ_(i−1). The analogous formula holds with γu.
proofSteps: Use determinant expansion for orthogonalized bases and exterior-power pairings.
All divisions are licensed by the preceding nonvanishing theorem.

items.name: Rational expression for all Hodge matrix entries
items.statement: In a fixed flat complex basis, every h_z(u,v) lies in the complexified fraction algebra O(x,y). Decompose u,v in the B-orthogonal adapted basis; its ith contribution is i^(2p_i−k) B(u,wtilde_i)B(wtilde_i,v)/B(wtilde_i,wtilde_i).
proofSteps: Entries of γ(z)=exp(zN)g(q) belong to the restricted-analytic polynomial algebra.
Apply the determinant/projection formulas, then the phase relation between B and the paper’s Hodge form.
Translate to the pinned conjugate-first convention only through the explicit conjugation comparison.

items.name: Rough monomial norm on a simultaneous Hodge-weight piece
items.statement: For a nonzero fixed vector u in a simultaneous complex piece I^(p,q₁,…,q_n), its squared Hodge norm is roughly monomial on a sufficiently deep ordered sector. The corresponding centered weight exponents are obtained by shifting p+q_j by the pure weight.
proofSteps: Compare the two adapted splittings using their common weight filtrations and a nonzero leading multigraded component.
Use the split norm asymptotics for two-sided monomial bounds, together with rationality of the entry.

items.name: Rough monomial norm of the transported vector
items.statement: For nonzero u in a simultaneous complex piece, the squared norm h_z(γ(z)u,γ(z)u) is roughly monomial, including the determinant vectors of the adapted flag in the induced exterior-power variations.
proofSteps: Use the same rational Gram expression for γu.
Combine twisted norm asymptotics with the relative perturbation comparison.
Apply the argument to the exterior-power Hodge structures used by the flag determinants.

items.name: Rough polynomial pairing of split vectors
items.statement: For u and v in simultaneous complex pieces, the real and imaginary parts of h_z(u,v) are roughly polynomial. Zero vectors give the zero function and require no roughly monomial assertion.
proofSteps: The absolute values of the adapted flag Gram determinants are roughly monomial.
Their signs/phases are fixed by the Hodge types; hence denominators can be expressed using nonvanishing rough monomials.
The numerator belongs to the polynomial coefficient algebra.

items.name: Rough polynomial Hodge form
items.statement: For any fixed u,v in the complex flat fibre, h_z(u,v) has roughly polynomial real and imaginary parts on an ordered sector after shrinking.
proofSteps: Expand u and v in the finite simultaneous splitting.
Use sesquilinearity and the ring closure laws.

items.name: Reduced forms and Siegel sets
items.statement: For a fixed ordered rational basis e and C, the set of (e,C)-reduced positive forms is semialgebraic and contained in a Siegel set of the positive-form symmetric space for its chosen compact. Conversely each such Siegel set lies in a reduced-form set for some basis and constant.

Check changes from rational bases to integral lattices and the determinant convention.

items.name: Basis change with determinant control and finite ordering
items.statement: Fix rational bases e,e′. If b is (e′,C′)-reduced and ∏b(e_i,e_i)≤C det(b in e), then the off-diagonal bounds in basis e hold with a constant depending only on e,e′,C,C′. After ordering e by increasing b-length, the full reducedness conditions hold with a uniform enlarged constant. Only finitely many permutations are used.

proofSteps: Use the integral/rational change-of-basis matrix and the determinant-product bound to control off-diagonal entries.
Retain a finite permutation of the basis to impose the diagonal ordering.

The quantitative off-diagonal proof still needs the original reduction-theory audit.

items.name: Bounded product of adapted diagonal norms
items.statement: For a rational basis adapted to the simultaneous centered monodromy weight filtrations, the product of its squared Hodge norms is bounded by a constant times the determinant of the Hodge form. Centered weights cancel in the top exterior power.
proofSteps: Multiply the monomial norm bounds for the adapted basis.
Use the centered-weight sum zero on the determinant representation and the fixed polarization volume.
Keep any rational-basis determinant factor in the comparison constant.

items.name: One-variable period lift lies in a Siegel set
items.statement: For a unipotent local polarized period map and any R,η>0, its lift on {|Re z|≤R, Im z≥η} lies in one rational Siegel set for the compatible Hodge compact data.
proofSteps: Use Schmid’s one-variable SL₂-orbit asymptotic factorization in horospherical coordinates.
Its positive-root coordinates tend to one or infinity and its other factors stay bounded.
Enlarge the set to include the remaining compact strip segment.

items.name: Faithful representation compatible with the Hodge compact
items.statement: Choose a faithful rational polarized Hodge representation of the semisimple group used for D, possibly replacing the adjoint presentation by an appropriate central cover or by its adjoint representation. The induced map to the positive-form symmetric space has compatible maximal compacts and Cartan involutions; its preimage fibres include the compact K/M directions.
items.locator: §4.5, passage to positive definite forms; erratum§§1.4–1.5
proofSteps: Retain the group on which the chosen rational representation actually acts; an adjoint Mumford–Tate group need not act on the original standard lattice.
Construct the induced polarized variation and Hodge metric, and verify Cartan compatibility.
Compare the arithmetic quotient under any finite central change of presentation.
items.note: This is an explicit representation/central-cover adapter, not an assumed embedding of every adjoint Mumford–Tate group into GL of the original fibre.

items.name: Reducedness along each rational-slope curve
items.statement: On every curve used by rational-curve-test, pullback of the local variation, after clearing rational slope denominators, has one-variable unipotent monodromy. Schmid’s theorem and the faithful representation give reducedness in some fixed curve-dependent rational basis; determinant control transfers the off-diagonal bounds to the chosen simultaneous basis.
proofSteps: Translate a rational-slope affine curve under q into a punctured-disk map with integer powers after a finite cover.
Apply the one-variable theorem and the corrected forward Siegel containment.
Use the determinant bound to transfer to the common basis; constants may depend on the curve.

items.name: Uniform reducedness up to finitely many basis permutations
items.statement: On a sufficiently deep ordered sector, the Hodge forms satisfy all off-diagonal reducedness bounds in one adapted rational basis with a single constant. Sorting its finitely many basis vectors pointwise gives finitely many reduced-form sets covering the image.
items.locator: §4.5, main claim with explicit finite permutations
proofSteps: Apply the curve test to each matrix entry relative to the positive diagonal norm.
Take a maximum over finitely many pairs for one constant.
Use determinant control and the finite set of orderings; a single ordering on the entire sector is not asserted.

items.name: Finite Siegel containment for a local period lift
items.statement: Let a polarized integral variation on (Δ*)^n have unipotent monodromy and lift Φtilde:H^n→D. For each R,η>0 its image on H^n_(R,η) is contained in a finite union of rational Siegel sets of D, all for the canonical Hodge compact. The multivariable assertion is finite union, not one set.
proofSteps: For each imaginary-order sector, use reducedness to cover the positive-form image by finitely many Siegel sets.
Use the corrected rational pullback theorem and the compact K/M fibre to obtain finitely many Siegel sets in D.

Extend the deep-sector argument to arbitrary positive η with finitely many buffered boundary-face charts and compact auxiliary parameters. The complement of a deep multivariable sector is not itself compact.
items.note: Uniform estimates with auxiliary parameters and the face-cover step remain an explicit proof interface.

items.name: Definability on a smaller punctured polydisk
items.statement: For a polarized integral variation on a punctured polydisk, there is a smaller radius ρ>0 such that its period map restricted to (Δ*_ρ)^n is R_an,exp-definable in the canonical target structure. Products with sufficiently small unpunctured disks and finite quasi-unipotent covers are included.
items.locator: Theorem4.1 as used after the shrinking in §4.2
proofSteps: Work on finitely many overlapping bounded angular sectors over the smaller polydisk.
Compose the definable lift with the quotient map on the finite Siegel cover.
Descend through sector coverings and finite power covers; include trivial-monodromy coordinates by their analytic extension.
items.note: The printed whole-open-polydisk formulation is not adopted without shrinking; see local-outer-boundary-obstruction.

items.name: Definability of the global period map
items.statement: For a pure polarized integral variation on a smooth complex quasi-projective S, its holomorphic period map to the associated torsion-free arithmetic Hodge manifold, with the canonical compact-dependent structure, is R_an,exp-definable relative to the algebraic definable structure on S.
proofSteps: Use a finite buffered cover of a normal-crossing compactification.
Apply the smaller-polydisk statement with compact auxiliary coordinates and finite étale level descent.
Glue the finitely many definable graphs.

items.name: Why shrinking the local polydisk is necessary
items.statement: The assertion that every local period map on the entire open punctured unit disk is definable is false. Let f(z)=exp(−(1+z)/(1−z)) and τ(z)=2i+εf(z) for sufficiently small ε>0. This gives a weight-one polarized integral variation with trivial monodromy and image in an injective uniformization chart. The fibre f=e^(−1) contains z_n=2πin/(2+2πin), n≠0, accumulating at the outer boundary 1, so it is not o-minimal-definable.
items.locator: Audit example for Theorem4.1 and its explicit shrinking in the proof
proofSteps: For |z|<1, Re((1+z)/(1−z))>0, so |f|<1 and τ stays in a small ball in H.
The trivial rank-two lattice with Hodge line span(τ,1) defines the standard polarized weight-one variation; transversality is automatic.
Compute the infinite discrete fibre above, which contradicts o-minimality. Restrictions to any smaller closed disk have an analytic buffer.
items.note: Derived scope check, not a published author erratum and not a counterexample to Theorem1.3 on an algebraic base.

items.name: Canonical structure on the symmetric space quotient
items.statement: Let X be the G-homogeneous space of maximal compact subgroups. Transporting the fixed-K structure on Γ\G/K along gK↦gKg⁻¹ gives a semialgebraic structure on Γ\X independent of K. More generally an equivariant map Y→X specifies compatible choices at every point of a homogeneous G-space Y.
proofSteps: Changing the base point changes K by conjugacy and the corresponding identification by right translation.
Apply the fixed-K/right-translation Siegel comparison; do not conclude that structures on a fixed Γ\G/M are independent of K.

items.name: Definable complex analytic Chow theorem
items.statement: If S is a complex algebraic variety and Z⊂S^an is a closed complex analytic subset definable in an o-minimal expansion of R_an, then Z is algebraic. Here it suffices to take S smooth and quasi-projective. Closedness and compatibility with the algebraic definable structure are hypotheses.
proofSteps: Import the Peterzil–Starchenko definable Chow theorem with the displayed hypotheses.
The original proof is a remaining prerequisite audit; projective analytic Chow alone does not provide this nonproper theorem.

items.name: A holomorphic map with algebraic graph is regular
items.statement: For smooth complex algebraic S and a separated complex algebraic Y, a holomorphic map f:S^an→Y^an whose graph is algebraic comes from a regular algebraic map. The projection of its reduced algebraic graph to S is an isomorphism.
proofSteps: Analytic graph projection is an isomorphism and has singleton fibres.
Establish the algebraic quasi-finite/birational comparison, then use normality of S and the absence of missing analytic points to identify the open immersion with S.
items.note: Precise algebraic/analytic comparison supplier and full proof still require decomposition; no properness of S is assumed.

items.name: Arithmetic and algebraic definability on Hermitian quotients
items.statement: For a torsion-free arithmetic quotient of a Hermitian symmetric domain, the identity between the fixed-canonical-K arithmetic definable structure and its Baily–Borel algebraic definable structure is R_an,exp-definable. This is not in general R_an-definable.
proofSteps: Obtain definability of uniformization on a finite semialgebraic Siegel fundamental set in the algebraic target.
Use definable quotient descent to compare the two structures.
items.note: Acquire KUY16 proof and establish that its use here is independent of the Borel algebraicity theorem being reproved; do not silently identify the two structures.

items.name: Borel algebraicity via period-map definability
items.statement: Every holomorphic map from a smooth complex algebraic variety to a torsion-free arithmetic quotient of a Hermitian symmetric domain is algebraic with respect to its algebraic quotient structure.
proofSteps: On quasi-projective source opens realize the map through the homogeneous adjoint polarized variation; horizontality is automatic in the Hermitian case.
Use the algebraic-target structure comparison before applying definable Chow to the graph.
Convert the graph into a regular map and glue over the algebraic source.

items.name: Proper special Hodge subvarieties
items.statement: A special Hodge subvariety relevant to the exceptional Hodge locus is the image of an arithmetic Hodge morphism from a Hodge subdatum with strictly smaller generic Mumford–Tate group (allowing connected components and rational translates). The exceptional qualifier excludes the identity image of the generic Hodge datum.

items.name: Closed analytic images of Hodge morphisms
items.statement: An arithmetic Hodge morphism associated to a Hodge subdatum has proper map onto its image, and its image is a closed complex analytic subvariety of the target Hodge manifold. Its source and target are taken at compatible arithmetic levels.
proofSteps: Prove the arithmetic properness assertion at compatible levels using reduction theory.
Use the proper holomorphic image theorem to obtain a closed analytic image.
items.note: The precise properness and analytic image inputs have not been fully source-decomposed; they cannot be replaced by definability alone.

items.name: Definability of each special Hodge subvariety
items.statement: Each special Hodge subvariety is semialgebraic-definable in the canonical arithmetic structure on the target Hodge manifold. This does not assert algebraicity of a generally nonalgebraic Hodge manifold.
proofSteps: The canonical Hodge compact subgroups satisfy the corrected morphism hypotheses.
Project the graph of the semialgebraic-definable arithmetic morphism to its image.

items.name: Countable supply of exceptional Hodge subdata
items.statement: For a fixed rational polarized Hodge datum there are countably many rational tensor conditions and rational Hodge subdata that can cut out exceptional Mumford–Tate groups, including their rational translates and arithmetic connected components. Their special images cover the exceptional Hodge locus.
proofSteps: Tensor constructions on a finite-dimensional rational vector space have countably many rational tensors.
Use stabilizers of finite tensor families to enumerate rational subgroups and then the Hodge-subdatum condition.
Separate the tensors already of Hodge type at the generic point from exceptional tensors.
items.note: The tensor-stabilizer/Hodge-subdatum correspondence and component enumeration are still prerequisite proof leaves.

items.name: Algebraicity of each special-locus pullback
items.statement: For a pure polarized integral variation over smooth complex quasi-projective S with period map Φ, the preimage of any special Hodge subvariety is a closed algebraic subvariety of S.
proofSteps: Closed analyticity follows from the holomorphic period map and the closed analytic target image.
Its graph and the definable special image give a definable preimage in the algebraic structure of S.
Apply definable analytic Chow.

items.name: Algebraicity of the exceptional Hodge locus
items.statement: The exceptional Hodge locus of a pure polarized integral variation over a smooth complex quasi-projective variety is a countable union of closed irreducible algebraic subvarieties. Each special-image pullback has finitely many algebraic irreducible components. The countable union need not itself be definable or closed.
proofSteps: Enumerate the proper special Hodge images corresponding to exceptional tensors.
Apply algebraicity separately to each pullback.
Take the finite irreducible decomposition of each algebraic pullback and their countable union; never invoke closure of definable sets under countable unions.

items.name: Finiteness of definable connected components
items.statement: Every definable subset of R^n in an o-minimal expansion of the real field has finitely many connected components, each definable. This extends to finite definable atlases.
proofSteps: Use o-minimal cell decomposition from LD.6.
Finite atlas gluing preserves finiteness.

items.name: Existing planned normal-crossing compactification
items.statement: A smooth complex quasi-projective variety has a smooth projective compactification whose reduced boundary is a simple normal-crossing divisor.
proofSteps: Import the characteristic-zero compactification and resolution construction from its existing owner.

items.name: Proper holomorphic image theorem
items.statement: The image of a proper holomorphic map of complex analytic spaces is a closed complex analytic subset of the target.
proofSteps: Use the analytic-space/coherent-ideal foundations of ComplexComparisonPartII C0; the full Remmert proof remains a source-audit leaf.

items.name: Uniform arithmetic lattices have no nontrivial unipotents
items.statement: A cocompact lattice in the real points of a semisimple group contains no nonidentity unipotent element.
proofSteps: Import the precise lattice theorem; combined with quasi-unipotence it forces finite local monodromy.
items.note: Original Raghunathan proof not acquired in this checkpoint.

items.name: Restricted-analytic definability for a compact Hodge target
items.statement: If the arithmetic Hodge target of a pure polarized integral variation on smooth complex quasi-projective S is compact, then its period map is R_an-definable. At a torsion-free target level, finite local monodromy in the adjoint target is trivial; after the needed finite level cover the period map extends across a normal-crossing compactification.
proofSteps: Cocompactness and quasi-unipotence give finite monodromy at every boundary component.
At the appropriate finite cover use the extension theorem for trivial monodromy, retaining the distinction between the original variation and the adjoint target.
An analytic map on the compactification has an R_an-definable graph in finite buffered charts, and finite descent recovers the original map.
items.note: Finite global level-cover and extension details remain to be decomposed; no claim of a compact-target proof independent of the Hodge degeneration inputs.

For connected semisimple rational G, torsion-free arithmetic Γ, connected compact M and a chosen maximal compact K containing M, construct the R_alg-definable structure on Γ\G/M characterized by fixed-K Siegel charts. For neat Γ construct the general Borel–Serre analytic manifold with corners and prove that its compactification induces the same R_an structure on the interior. Specializing M=K must recover ALS.2. Decompose the semialgebraic homogeneous quotient, finite proper equivalence relation, local slice refinement, boundary gluing and nonsurjective/surjective morphism adapters. routes.title: Hodge structures (pure, mixed, and polarized), Part II: degeneration, period maps and Hodge loci
routes.reason: Upstream HodgeStructures L0–L3 supplies pure/mixed structures, polarizations, Deligne splitting and period-domain points, all largely built. It explicitly reserves the period-domain manifold structure for a successor. The multivariable degeneration, non-Hermitian domain geometry and period-map/locus theorems therefore extend this direction.
routes.brief: Import Hodge structures (pure, mixed, and polarized) (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HodgeStructures L0–L3) through the pinned carriers, positive Hodge form, Weil operator and Deligne decomposition; import the general polarized-variation definition from ShimuraData D3, normal-crossing compactifications from AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.7d, rational reduction from AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.3, analytic spaces from ComplexComparisonPartII C0, and definable geometry/Chow from LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory LD.6. Use ArithmeticQuotientDefinability for corrected fixed-K quotient structures. Construct the complex manifold and compact dual on the existing period-point carrier, the canonical Hodge Cartan involution and compatible Hodge morphisms. Prove Theorem1.5: for a local unipotent pure polarized integral variation and any bounded real width R and positive height η, the lifted period map on H_(R,η)^n lies in finitely many fixed-canonical-K Siegel sets. Establish nilpotent extension, centered monodromy weights, simultaneous rational and complex splittings, both Kashiwara norm estimates, the horizontal correction, indefinite Gram determinant formulas, rough entries and finite-permutation reducedness. Establish the faithful adjoint/central-cover representation adapter before using SL(V) reduction. Then prove Theorem1.3: every such variation on smooth complex quasi-projective S has an R_an,exp-definable period map. Local use must shrink and buffer disks and cover angular seams. Finally prove Theorem1.6: the exceptional Hodge locus is a countable union of closed irreducible algebraic subvarieties, through closed analytic proper special images and definable Chow applied individually to their pullbacks. Exclude the generic identity subdatum; do not call the countable union definable. Supply Borel algebraicity only as an imported/alternative proof at ShimuraVarieties V3. Tests include zero monodromy, the zero-vector exclusion, weight shifts, conjugation conventions, a non-Hermitian domain, reversed reduced bases and the outer-boundary period-map example. Suggested later file: TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/Variation/DefinablePeriodMap.lean. Original analytic inputs and the curve-test domain repair remain open in this partial brief.
